All five agents also showed non-zero leakage after memory deletion. ★★★★ Notable: The authors audit privacy risks of long-term memory in five commercial AI agents using about 3800 multi-turn sessions, and propose a stealth memory injection technique.

entry.title: ParseGap: Testing Whether Coding Agents' Command Approvals Match What Shells Actually Run
entry.summary: ParseGap: Testing What Coding Agents Authorize and What Shells Execute arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper examines how LLM coding agents approve shell commands by parsing them against a policy and then passing the raw string to a shell, which can interpret it differently. The authors present ParseGap, a differential testing framework that runs commands through vendor checkers and GNU Bash 5.2 in an isolated container to flag approved commands with policy-violating effects. They also propose ShellPlan, which compiles a restricted Bash subset into a typed execution plan and dispatches it directly via execve without a shell. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors identify a dual-interpretation gap between command authorization and shell execution and propose ShellPlan, which dispatches plans via execve. The abstract reports tests across eight agent

entry.title: Adaptation or Poisoning? Security Risks of Conversational Test-Time Learning in LLMs
entry.summary: Adaptation or Poisoning? Security Risks of Conversational Test-Time Learning in Large Language Models arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper examines security risks of test-time learning in large language models, where a lightweight adapter is updated on user inputs during deployment. The authors introduce P-TAP, a query-only multi-turn attack that gradually poisons the session adapter through ordinary interactions so that a final harmful request is answered after the model is jailbroken. Across four open-weight instruction-tuned models, enabling updates raises attack success rates on average, and adapting on unrelated or same-topic benign text removes most of that increase. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose P-TAP, a query-only multi-turn attack poisoning session adapters via test-time updates; the paper reports attack success gains across four open-weight instruction-tuned models.

entry.title: NRSnooper: A passive sniffer that decodes live two-way traffic on commercial 5G networks
entry.summary: NRSnooper: Enabling Real-Time Bidirectional Traffic Decoding in Commercial 5G NR Networks arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper presents NRSnooper, a passive sniffer that decodes downlink control and bidirectional data traffic in commercial 5G NR networks in real time, including traffic from already-connected devices and after encrypted configuration updates. It learns reusable physical-layer configurations using an instrumented open-source UE, recovers connection identifiers from ongoing transmissions, and selects matching configurations through CRC-validated decoding, with a hybrid CPU-GPU pipeline for wideband processing. Evaluations on a testbed and two commercial networks report decoding 1.3x and 6.3x more control messages and 9.0x and 17.7x more downlink data blocks than using only unencrypted-signaling configurations. The system also achieves real-time bidirectional decoding on 100 MHz commercial NR channels. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors report real-time bidirectional 5G NR decoding of connected UEs using reusable configurations and CRC-validated selection, with large gains over unencrypted-signaling baselines on two comme

entry.title: Finding mismatches between RISC-V specs and zkVM constraints via obligation-guided fuzzing
entry.summary: Revealing Semantic Gaps in Zero-Knowledge Virtual Machines via Obligation-Targeted Semantic Fuzzing arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper studies security bugs in zero-knowledge virtual machines (zkVMs), where the constraint system fails to match the RISC-V instruction set, enabling forged proofs or preventing valid ones. The authors present Beak, a reinforcement-learning fuzzer that uses constraint obligations derived from the ISA specification to generate inputs, reward new obligation combinations, and guide witness tampering. Beak finds divergence bugs by comparing against a reference RISC-V emulator and underconstraint bugs by checking whether tampered witnesses are accepted. On six production RISC-V zkVMs it detects 25 of 37 known bugs and finds 14 previously unknown bugs, all disclosed and patched. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors guide reinforcement-learning fuzzing with constraint obligations from the RISC-V spec, reporting 25 of 37 known bugs and 14 new bugs across six production zkVMs.

entry.title: Ziv Meets Sumcheck: Zero-Knowledge Proofs for Floating-Point LLM Inference
entry.summary: Ziv Meets Sumcheck: Zero-Knowledge Proofs of Floating-Point LLM Inference arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper presents a zero-knowledge proof method that shows a language model produced a given output using floating-point arithmetic, without revealing the model. It avoids the difficulty of order-dependent rounding by proving a correctly rounded product of each dot product and extends the approach to every transformer layer. The authors implemented the system for the full forward pass of GPT-2 small, reporting 19 minutes to prove and 21 seconds to verify. ★★★★ Notable: The authors prove correctly rounded floating-point matrix products and report a full GPT-2 small forward pass proof, plus rejection of 236 attacks.

entry.title: Verification That Rejects Correct Machine Answers: Psychoacoustic Audio CAPTCHAs
entry.summary: When Being Wrong Is Right: Reverse-Capability Audio CAPTCHAs through Psychoacoustic Design arXiv · Nov 21, 2026The paper addresses audio CAPTCHAs being bypassed by large audio-language models by proposing reverse-capability verification, which selects challenges where human perceptual limits make the human-reference answer differ from the physical ground truth. Using psychoacoustic design, it builds two audio tasks, HIPI (classification) and YINGCHEN (counting), and their conjunctive composition. Tests across seven models and eight attacks show machine acceptance well below nine prior schemes, with human acceptance rates of 76% to 90%. ★★★★ Notable: The authors propose reverse-capability verification using psychoacoustics; they report reduced machine acceptance across seven LALMs and eight attacks, plus a human usability study.

entry.title: Explaining the 2020 Census privacy figure ε=19.61 through operationally equivalent pure-DP ε values
entry.summary: Reporting Differential Privacy Guarantees via Operationally Equivalent ǎrepsilon: What Does ǎrepsilon=19.61 Mean for the 2020 U.S. Census? arXiv · Nov 21, 2026The paper addresses the reported approximate differential privacy parameter ε=19.61 for the 2020 U.S. Census, which was derived from zCDP guarantees. It proposes the α-operationally equivalent ε, the smallest pure DP parameter giving the same power bound on distinguishing tests at a given significance level. For the P.L. 94-171 data, the zCDP guarantee yields values of about 4.25, 2.94, and 3.18 at significance levels of 1%, 5%, and 10%. The authors also show that converting to a single ADP pair produces power bounds near 1 at all three levels. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors propose alpha-operationally equivalent epsilon, converting ADP power bounds to pure DP parameters and characterizing extrema; they report values for the 2020 Census zCDP guarantee.

entry.title: Who Is Prompt-Injecting Coding Agents? Hidden AI-Directed Text on GitHub
entry.summary: Who Is Prompt-Injecting Coding Agents? An Empirical Study of Hidden AI-Directed Text on GitHub arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper presents a large-scale empirical study of hidden text on GitHub that human readers cannot see but AI coding agents receive in full. The authors analyzed roughly 145 million issues, pull requests, comments and README files, and validated 2,281 findings in issues, pull requests and comments, plus AI-directed hidden text in the READMEs of 107 repositories. The study identifies four uses: attacks on other parties' agents, defensive text that restricts agents, content override, and first-party orchestration through hidden markers. The authors also report offline replay results against five tested models and release their detection tool and findings. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors present the first large-scale study of hidden AI-directed text on GitHub, classifying four uses across about 145 million items and replaying attacks offline against five models.

entry.title: Zero-Trust Formal Methods: AI Agents Build Verified Checkers for Untrusted Solvers
entry.summary: Zero-Trust Formal Methods: AI Agents Build Verified Checkers for Untrusted Solvers arXiv · Nov 21, 2026The paper proposes a formal verification framework that trusts no component by default, including AI agents and SAT, SMT, and answer-set solvers. A solver answer is accepted only if a verified checker accepts its certificate, and all theories, proofs, and code are generated by AI, with specifications frozen after independent review. The authors built trust chains for SAT, SMT, and answer-set programming, certifying 3,726 SMT queries and accepting 15,662 answer-set proofs. They report soundness defects in three proof checkers, including drat-trim, and in five solvers, including clasp and z3. ★★★★★ Notable: The authors have AI agents generate all proofs and code, verifying SAT, SMT, and ASP solver certificates. They report 3,726 SMT and 15,662 ASP proofs checked and soundness defects in several solvers a

entry.title: Correct Verdict, Correct Reasoning? Testing Whether LLM Vulnerability Detectors Truly Understand Bugs
entry.summary: Right Verdict, Right Reason? An Execution-Grounded Study of Whether LLM Vulnerability Detectors Understand Vulnerabilities arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper tests whether large language models that detect software vulnerabilities truly understand them, using program execution as ground truth. For 515 C and C++ functions from BigVul and PrimeVul, the authors reproduced each vulnerability with a proof of concept and identified the faulting line and the statements the faulting run depended on. Five tests with non-understanding baselines were applied, and results show open-weight models did no better than chance at separating vulnerable functions from fixed versions, while commercial models localized faults beyond a keyword rule, though this advantage disappeared on newer vulnerabilities. The authors release their framework, per-function evidence, and an execution-confirmed counterfactual benchmark. ★★★★ Notable: The authors use program execution to build five understanding tests, each paired with a no-understanding baseline, and repeat the study on post-cutoff vulnerabilities.

entry.title: Praxis: A Practical Witness Encryption Scheme for NP Statements
entry.summary: Praxis: Practical Witness Encryption for NP arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper proposes Praxis, a witness encryption scheme that encrypts messages to NP statements so that only holders of a witness can decrypt. The authors prove extractability in the bilinear generic group and random oracle models under Module-SIS, and give a concrete instantiation that encrypts to a Groth16 verifier on BN254. They report ciphertext size, encryption and decryption costs at 100-bit security, and state that correctness and extraction were proven in Lean 4 for these parameters. ★★★★ Notable: The authors report a practical NP witness encryption scheme improving on a rank-gap template, with lower ciphertext and encryption costs than prior constructions.

entry.title: Optimal User-Level Private Optimization and Mean Estimation with Heavy-Tailed Data
entry.summary: Optimal User-Level Private Stochastic Convex Optimization and Mean Estimation with Heavy Tails arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper studies stochastic convex optimization with heavy-tailed gradients under user-level differential privacy, which protects each user's full set of samples. Instead of a uniform Lipschitz bound, it assumes only bounds on the second and k-th moments of the random sample Lipschitz parameters. The authors characterize the minimax optimal excess population risk up to logarithmic factors, and their algorithm reaches this rate with only about O~(1/ε) users. The work also gives tight bounds for user-level private mean estimation and removes an extra d/ε user requirement from a prior directional-moment result. ★★★★ Notable: The authors characterize minimax optimal excess risk under heavy tails and user-level privacy, and improve mean estimation bounds, mostly within a subfield.

entry.title: Code-Based Message Authentication with Statistical Guarantees via Coordinate Selection and Masking
entry.summary: Code-Based Message Authentication with Statistical Guarantees via Coordinate Selection and Masking arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper studies message authentication over a public channel against an adversary with unbounded computing power, focusing on low-complexity uses. It builds authentication tags from binary linear codes already used for error correction, selecting several coordinates to support different tag lengths. The authors analyze how three selection methods affect guarantees against impersonation and substitution attacks, and evaluate first-order Reed-Muller and BCH dual subcodes.

entry.title: Privacy cost of writing audit records before future queries are known
entry.summary: The Privacy Cost of Writing an Audit Receipt Before Its Context Is Known arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper studies how an audit recorder can enable exact recovery through a small private index without knowing which questions future readers will ask. It uses a recursion on question partitions to generate decision trees, their costs, and price equations, and gives the optimal identification probability as a function of follow-up budget on uniform binary linear event spaces. The results are checked on 960 local TLS sessions.

entry.title: Preflight: Checking AI Software Dependencies Before Running Them
entry.summary: Preflight: Agentic Last-Mile Verification for AI Software Supply Chains arXiv · Nov 24, 2026The paper presents Preflight, a tool that verifies Python dependencies before execution, scoped to a specific downstream program. It extracts symbols the application references, generates and validates function-level test harnesses, runs the artifacts in a restricted environment, and records behavioral fingerprints. Evaluated on four real supply-chain incidents and 100 benign packages, it returned malicious verdicts in four incident contexts and clean verdicts for all benign packages, with zero observed false positives.

entry.title: CenShaper: Reshaping Proxy Traffic to Evade Censorship
entry.summary: CenShaper: Shaping Proxy Traffic for Censorship Circumvention arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper addresses how censorship circumvention proxies can make their traffic resemble legitimate Internet traffic so that deep packet inspection cannot detect them. The authors analyzed about 12 million TLS connections at a regional ISP and found that individual servers differ substantially from the broader TLS population. They present CenShaper, which trains a shared generative model and adapts it to make each proxy imitate a chosen TLS server. In end-to-end tests, it reduced TLS-over-TLS detection from over 85% to about 3% at a 1% false positive rate.

entry.title: Airlock: A Hardware-Isolated Sandbox to Contain and Govern Rogue AI Agents
entry.summary: Airlock: Robust Sandboxing and Governance of Rogue Agents arXiv · Nov 24, 2026This paper proposes Airlock, an architecture that pairs each agent's virtual machine with a separate Airlock virtual machine, both running in hardware-isolated Trusted Execution Environments. The Airlock VM mediates all of the agent's network and storage operations, so network and filesystem policies and credential protection remain effective even if the agent VM is fully compromised, and the host is removed from the agent's I/O path. The authors implement and evaluate the system on a Radxa development board, reporting filesystem performance and small-message network latency losses under 15% and a network bandwidth drop of half or more.

entry.title: Intent-checked argument mediation to block trusted but unauthorized tool-call values in LLM agents
entry.summary: Intent-Conditioned Argument Mediation for Tool-Using LLM Agents: Blocking Trusted-but-Unauthorized Arguments arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper proposes IntentFlow, a mediation layer between an LLM agent's planner and its tools that checks authority-bearing arguments against an intent contract and a provenance policy. On a 200-attack synthetic benchmark, attack success drops from 50.5% with provenance alone to 12.0%. It also blocks 50 trusted-but-unauthorized attacks that provenance-only mediation executes.

entry.title: Meeting Cybersecurity Law: NIS2 Challenges and a Large Company's Case Study
entry.summary: Complying with Cybersecurity Legislation: NIS2 Challenges and Industry Case Study arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper describes how a large European enterprise worked to align with the NIS2 Directive, the revised EU-wide cybersecurity law that entered into force on 16 January 2023. It presents a systematic method for interpreting the directive's provisions and turning them into concrete technical and organizational measures. The paper discusses challenges in practice, including supply chains and third parties and zero-trust principles, and provides reusable artifacts.

entry.title: Bug Bounty Programs in the AI Era: Platform Anti-Spam Rules and Vendor Profit
entry.summary: Bug Bounty Programs in the AI Era: How Does Platform Anti-Spam Friction Affect Vendor Profitability? arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper examines whether bug bounty platform rules, such as proof-of-concept requirements introduced since 2023 to counter floods of AI-generated low-quality reports, benefit the vendors running programs on them. Building on a 2024 model by Gal-Or, Hydari, and Telang, the authors add a vendor triage cost per report and a researcher participation cost. They find a threshold in an effective triage-burden parameter: below it the rules lower vendor profit, and above it they raise profit. Because attackers do not use the platform, the participation cost falls only on researchers, so fewer take part, reducing bug-finding coverage and increasing breach damage, while the vendor's triage costs decline.

entry.title: POMA: Step-by-step evaluation of base LLMs in exploiting software vulnerabilities
entry.summary: POMA: Beyond Final Flags -- Process-Level Evaluation of Base LLMs in Vulnerability Exploitation arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper introduces POMA (Pwn-Oriented Model Assessment), a process-level method and platform for evaluating base large language models on vulnerability exploitation under a unified execution setup. Instead of only scoring pass or fail, it measures intermediate states and transitions from runtime evidence. Four frontier models were tested on 55 CTF Pwn challenges and 10 real-world vulnerability reproduction tasks, showing capability declining along the exploitation chain. The authors argue this provides a basis for more trustworthy capability assessment and vulnerability-agent design.

entry.title: CyberDualEval: A Benchmark Measuring Dual-Use Cyber Risks in Frontier Language Models
entry.summary: CyberDualEval: Measuring Dual-Use Cyber Risks in Frontier Language Models arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper introduces CyberDualEval, a benchmark of 430 vulnerable tasks for measuring dual-use cyber risk in frontier language models. Each task is split into security analysis, proof-of-concept generation, and exploit generation, and annotated with a Task Weaponization Score estimating the remaining effort needed to turn outputs into misuse. Ten closed- and open-weight models are evaluated on compliance and task performance. Results show existing frontier models are overly cautious and fail to balance helping with safe requests and refusing risky ones, while recent open-weight models rarely refuse and show strong accuracy on risky requests.

entry.title: Queuing for Secrets: Model-Based Remote Timing Attacks
entry.summary: Queuing for Secrets: Model-Based Remote Timing Attacks arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper proposes a stochastic framework for remote timing attacks that combines queuing models with Bayesian statistics. The attacker knows the service time distributions of two request classes and tries to tell them apart from observed response times despite noise from other workloads. Experiments on popular websites show it outperforms deterministic-service-time formal methods and existing empirical techniques, with less tuning than earlier formal approaches.

entry.title: Noise analysis for polynomial evaluation in the BGV encryption scheme
entry.summary: From Dependent Ciphertexts to Sharp Bounds for Polynomial Evaluation in BGV arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper analyzes noise growth in the BGV scheme, a fully homomorphic encryption method, under average-case assumptions that account for correlations from keys and dependencies between ciphertexts. The authors propose new variance estimates for noise in homomorphic additions and multiplications and extend the framework to polynomial evaluation. Their estimates differ from experiments by less than 1.2 bits, and using them to choose initial parameters yields about 11.5% smaller ciphertext moduli than OpenFHE.

entry.title: Does the database engine, the model, or a guard layer decide how much damage an AI agent's database mistake causes?
entry.summary: When an AI agent makes a mistake in a database, what decides the damage? arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper examines what determines the damage when an AI agent makes a mistake against a database: the model, a guard layer in front of the database, or the database engine itself. The study has two layers, one applying 22 fixed canonical mistakes to four relational engines by script, and one running small open-weight models as tool-calling agents across nine engines. It reports that out of the box, engines differ less in what a mistake destroys than in what they allow to be undone.

entry.title: WEPWAWET-CORE: A hardware-resident post-quantum signature design for spacecraft avionics
entry.summary: WEPWAWET-CORE: A Hardware-Resident ML-DSA Architecture with Fabric-Generated, Fabric-Sealed Keys for Post-Quantum Avionics arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper presents WEPWAWET-CORE, a hardware-resident implementation of the ML-DSA (FIPS 204) quantum-resistant signature algorithm on an XCZU3EG device at 300 MHz. Keys are generated and kept inside the hardware fabric, off the processor bus, and the full rejection loop runs on chip. Processor-side signing cost drops to 0.53 ms. In tests under NASA JPL's F Prime framework, two nodes exchanged 3,575 signed frames, all were accepted, and no attitude-control deadline was missed.

entry.title: Bounded Autonomy: Trust-Anchored Defense Against Resource-Exhaustion Attacks on LLM Agents
entry.summary: Bounded Autonomy: A Trust-Anchored Defense Against Resource-Exhaustion Attacks on Tool-Augmented LLM Agents arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper addresses the vulnerability of tool-augmented LLM agents to resource-exhaustion attacks that inflate token consumption. It proposes a trust-anchored closed-loop defense with four phases: certificate-guided orchestration, calibrated one-time node budgeting, Gateway-based runtime enforcement, and bounded recovery via a shared non-resettable recovery pool. The authors report that the framework bounds cumulative token use and mitigates amplification attacks while preserving benign task utility under trusted execution assumptions.

entry.title: ArguShield: Enforcing Minimum-Necessary Disclosure in Tool-Calling LLM Agents
entry.summary: ArguShield: Enforcing Minimum-Necessary Disclosure in Tool-Calling LLM Agents arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper presents ArguShield, a mediation layer that intercepts proposed tool calls before execution and evaluates each value using Value Provenance, Task Relevance, and Disclosure Boundary signals. It releases justified values, defers those needing user confirmation, and withholds values outside the permitted scope. Four tool-calling models were tested on ArgPrivBench, a 120-task benchmark spanning Travel, Shopping, and Healthcare. ArguShield reduced unauthorized silent release to 9% on Standard tasks and 6% on High-risk tasks while preserving recoverable task success under simulated user confirmation.

entry.title: PseuDRAGON: Knowledge-Guided Local LLMs for Pseudonymizing Financial Data in Closed Networks
entry.summary: PseuDRAGON: Knowledge-Guided Local LLMs for Financial-Data Pseudonymization in Closed Networks arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper presents PseuDRAGON, a system for pseudonymizing financial data in closed networks using local language models. It stores confirmed judgments and corrections outside the fixed model and reuses them through exact-name lookup and learned rules. Tests on 92 columns from one institution show rules raised reusable labels from 75 to 83 without reuse errors when all training judgments were available.

entry.title: AutoClip-DPZO: A practical method for automatically choosing clipping thresholds when fine-tuning LLMs with differentially private zeroth-order optimization
entry.summary: AutoClip-DPZO: Practical Private Clipping Selection for Differentially Private Zeroth-Order LLM Fine-Tuning arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper proposes AutoClip-DPZO, a method that automatically selects the clipping threshold C for differentially private zeroth-order optimization used to fine-tune large language models. It reduces the selection to private quantile estimation, where the target quantile depends only on public privacy and training parameters, avoiding repeated fine-tuning searches. Experiments show utility comparable to the optimal C with negligible extra overhead.

entry.title: A quantum-resistant, PUF-based authentication and key agreement scheme for drone networks
entry.summary: Quantum-Resilient, PUF-Based, and Anonymity-Preserving Authentication and Key Agreement Scheme for UAV Networks arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper presents a lightweight authentication and key agreement protocol for Internet of Drones environments. It combines CRYSTALS-Kyber, dynamic challenge scrambling, fuzzy extractors, and PUF-based identity binding to provide post-quantum security and hardware-rooted trust. The authors evaluate the scheme through formal security analysis, ProVerif verification, informal attack analysis, and communication, computation, and storage cost comparisons.

entry.title: Real-time ultrasound watermarking to help detect voice scams during smartphone calls
entry.summary: Ultrasound Watermark: Real-time Acoustic Watermarking against Voice Scams on Smartphones arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper presents Ultrasound Watermark, a framework that runs on smartphones during live calls to protect against voice impersonation. The phone emits ultrasonic signals with its built-in speaker and microphone, captures reflections from the caller's facial articulatory movements, and fuses these motion features with outgoing speech to create a dynamic watermark. The system adds less than 200 ms of latency and requires no extra hardware, and it was implemented on iOS and Android.

entry.title: LaTSEC: lattice-based threshold signatures with built-in non-interactive identification of misbehaving signers and low per-party storage
entry.summary: LaTSEC: Lattice-Based Threshold Signatures with Native Non-Interactive Identifiable Abort and Compact Per-Party Storage arXiv · Nov 23, 2026The paper presents LaTSEC, a three-round lattice-based threshold signature scheme in which each party holds one small signing share and one public abort key used to verify its partial signature directly. It builds on SEC, a ramp everywhere-short secret sharing scheme, so each party stores a single short share rather than several. The authors prove correctness, identifiable-abort security, and threshold unforgeability under the standard MLWE and MSIS assumptions.

entry.title: EnvTrap: A Study of Environment-Only Attacks on Embodied AI That Ignore Action Consequences
entry.summary: EnvTrap: Revealing the Environment-Only Attack Surface in Embodied AI via Consequence-Blind Action Execution arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper studies a way to attack physical AI agents by rearranging objects in their environment, without changing instructions or accessing the models. The authors introduce EnvTrap, a diagnostic pipeline that builds paired safe, trap, and benign-but-misleading scenarios. Environment-only perturbations raised hazardous-action rates to an average of 83.4% across five action policies, while models stayed near chance on consequence prediction and humans performed well. The authors also propose a consequence-aware defense that substantially reduces trap trigger rates.

entry.title: Antiphony: A Dual-Process Agent for Deepfake Video Detection with Real-Video Calibration
entry.summary: Antiphony: A Dual-Process Agent for Deepfake Video Detection with Real-Video Calibration arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper presents Antiphony, a framework for detecting deepfake videos that fuses scores from four visual expert detectors. Authentic videos serve as a shared reference to calibrate the fusion and decision threshold, so no target deepfakes are needed. Videos near the threshold are examined by a tool-using multimodal investigator that contributes an extra fusion score. Across six benchmark protocols, it achieves a mean score of 88.3%, and it outperforms ARGUS by 3.6 balanced-accuracy points on FaceVid's 20 unseen generators.

entry.title: Conartist: Adaptive agent-based red-teaming of computer-using agents against multi-step prompt injection
entry.summary: Conartist: Adaptive Agentic Red-Teaming of Computer-Using Agents against Multi-Step Prompt Injection arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper presents Conartist, a two-stage adaptive prompt injection framework that tests the security of computer-using agents. It first uses a goal-pollution strategy to embed malicious steps into legitimate task workflows so they pass consistency checks, then refines its deception based on risk-auditing feedback. Experiments across five backbone models report attack success rates of 32.12% and 66.67% on two benchmarks, and the authors identify seven exploitable patterns in the Openclaw agent.

entry.title: How automated AI red-team attacks become less varied during reinforcement learning training
entry.summary: Tracing Attacker Diversity Reduction in Adaptive LLM Red Teaming arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper examines why reinforcement learning makes automated red teaming of large language models use a narrower set of attacks. The authors test six mechanisms across three experimental arms over twenty-four iterations. They find that a frozen defender narrows attack diversity earlier, and that defender updates delay but do not prevent the narrowing.

entry.title: Packing Stern into L2: GPU-accelerated attack recovering high-codimension binary Goppa private keys
entry.summary: Packing Stern into L2: GPU-Accelerated Primal-Shortened ISD for High-Codimension Binary Goppa Key Recovery arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper presents a GPU-accelerated primal-shortened information-set decoding method for recovering private keys of binary Goppa codes at high codimension. The authors compress hash-table entries into a single 16-byte unit, share lookup tables within GPU L2 cache, and batch random systematic reductions. They report recovering keys for four Track-2 challenges, with runtimes and GPU-hour costs given for TII-228, TII-237 and TII-235. The authors state that these results do not demonstrate practical recovery against Classic McEliece parameters with mt ≥ 768.

entry.title: Comparing Machine Learning Classifiers for Lightweight IoT Intrusion Detection with Fewer Features
entry.summary: Comparative Analysis of Machine Learning Classifiers for Lightweight IoT Intrusion Detection Using Feature Reduction arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper presents a lightweight binary intrusion detection framework for IoT networks, built on an approximately balanced dataset derived from CICIoT2023 with attack labels merged into Benign and Malicious classes. Features were ranked using Information Gain Ratio and Gini Decrease to produce reduced subsets of 38 down to 3 features. Five classifiers were compared with 5-fold cross-validation, and Random Forest performed best overall. The 20-feature subset reached 99.1% accuracy and 0.982 MCC, matching the full-feature model with about 47.4% fewer features.

entry.title: MobileGrail: A compact on-device safety guardrail for mobile GUI agents
entry.summary: MobileGrail: Learning Compact Guardrails for On-Device deployable Mobile GUI Agent Safety arXiv · Nov 23, 2026MobileGrail is a safety guardrail model that runs on the device itself, reviewing each action a mobile GUI agent proposes before it executes, so screen contents need not be sent to cloud servers. It keeps a recurrent task state of the evidence later safety decisions depend on, and learns "unsafe" and "block" labels to time interventions precisely. On the offline MobileVeto benchmark, the Qwen3.5-2B-based model intercepts 76.2% of violations while cutting premature interventions to 5.2%. Quantized to 4 bits, it runs on a Snapdragon 8 Elite with a median latency of 4.7 s.

entry.title: Defending 5G networks against nested GTP attacks with a closed-loop eBPF system
entry.summary: Mitigating Nested GTP Attacks: A Closed-Loop eBPF Defense for 5G and Beyond Networks arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper proposes a closed-loop defense using eBPF and XDP to detect and mitigate nested GTP-U attacks in 5G and beyond networks. The framework has three parts: an in-kernel XDP detection and drop module, a user-space telemetry agent, and a multi-threaded control-plane mitigation orchestrator. The authors evaluated it on a sliced 5G testbed built with Free5GC, UERANSIM, and Containerlab. Results show malicious packets are dropped at line rate, and under a 10,000 packets-per-second cross-slice flood, victim slices keep baseline performance with minimal impact on user throughput and round-trip time.

entry.title: A lightweight method that filters out hidden backdoor triggers in AI inference chips
entry.summary: Lightweight Spectral Subspace Filtering for Trojan-Resilient AI Inference Engines arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper addresses backdoor attacks on deep neural networks running on AI inference engines, where hidden triggers cause malicious behavior while keeping normal accuracy high. It proposes a training-free framework that uses Singular Value Decomposition to find the dominant malicious subspace in latent features and projects activations to suppress it at inference time. Experiments across CNN and transformer models, including ViT, show a large reduction in attack success rate while maintaining high clean accuracy.

entry.title: Using Quantum Annealing to Shrink the Search Space for Large-Scale Shortest Paths
entry.summary: Quantum-Annealing-Assisted Search-Space Reduction for Large-Scale Shortest-Path Computation arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper examines whether quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) can reduce the work needed to find verified shortest paths in large weighted graphs. The authors compare block-based overlays with direct Dijkstra search on synthetic graphs and the New York road network, using simulated annealing on classical processors. The overlay reduced arc inspections in the final search in many cases, but once overheads were included, every tested case took longer per query than direct Dijkstra. The authors conclude that any benefit depends on whether the search savings outweigh the cost of obtaining and verifying local paths.

entry.title: Data contamination at the operating point: overlapping identities inflate low-FMR face recognition accuracy
entry.summary: Contamination at the Operating Point: Train-Test Identity Overlap Inflates Low-FMR Face Recognition Accuracy by an Order of Magnitude arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper examines bias in evaluating face verification systems at low false match rates (FMR), where deployed systems operate. The authors find that widely used benchmarks share identities with training corpora and show that removing contaminated test identities raises the false non-match rate by growing multiples as FMR decreases. They also measure the effective number of independent impostor comparisons in IJB-C and build a zero-overlap evaluation protocol.

entry.title: Adjusting Dimension Mid-Flight for Quantum Key Sharing over Airborne Links
entry.summary: Feed-Forward Dimension Control for High-Dimensional Quantum Key Distribution over Time-Varying Airborne Free-Space Links arXiv · Nov 23, 2026This paper proposes a controller that sets the dimension, acceptance thresholds, and key length of each block in high-dimensional quantum key distribution, using only public data from earlier blocks. It is evaluated on a simulated orbital-angular-momentum entanglement link between an aircraft and a ground station under varying turbulence. The recalibrated controller keeps at least 98.8% of the best fixed-dimension key in each scenario, and tests on a superconducting quantum processor show device errors can change the best daytime dimension.

entry.title: RSWP: SO(3)-equivariant watermarking that stays robust for panoramic images
entry.summary: RSWP: Robust SO(3)-Equivariant Watermarking for Panoramic Images arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper addresses robust watermarking for panoramic images, where spherical content and flat representations do not match and existing methods break under 3D viewing rotations. It proposes RSWP, which uses icosahedral group theory to split sphere rotations into local planar rotations and facet permutations, embedding watermarks into discrete facets. An equivariant feature extractor and a permutation-invariant sorting module decode the watermark, allowing blind retrieval from partial 2D renderings. The authors report state-of-the-art robustness to continuous SO(3) rotations and viewport transformations with high visual fidelity.

entry.title: NPUFHE: An Efficient CKKS Execution System for Ascend NPUs
entry.summary: NPUFHE: An Efficient CKKS Execution System for Ascend NPUs arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper presents NPUFHE, an end-to-end CKKS fully homomorphic encryption system optimized for Ascend NPUs, aimed at making encrypted computation practical for privacy-preserving AI. It introduces Boundary-Optimized NTT, Compact Shoup encoding for halving evaluation-key representation, and Cost-Aware Parallel Tiling to address tail load imbalance. On one Ascend 910B4, the authors report 0.95 s for full-packing CKKS bootstrapping, 9.87 s per image for encrypted CIFAR-10 ResNet-20 inference, and 19.81 ms amortized per image for encrypted MNIST inference.

entry.title: DuetFHE: A GPU compiler for dual-lane nonlinear circuits in encrypted CKKS inference
entry.summary: DuetFHE: Compiling Dual-Lane Nonlinear Circuits for Complex-Packed CKKS Inference arXiv · Nov 22, 2026The paper presents DuetFHE, a GPU compiler for complex-packed CKKS homomorphic encryption that handles two real data streams stored in the real and imaginary lanes. It uses a phase transformation to square both lanes independently with a single ciphertext multiplication and reuses these dual-lane squares in polynomial activations and bootstrapping. On one RTX 5090, it speeds up four polynomial activations by 1.60 to 1.79 times over direct evaluation on two real ciphertexts. For two-image AESPA ResNet-20 inference, it achieves a 1.97 times end-to-end speedup over the fastest tested EasyFHE batched baseline.

entry.title: SWIFT: A Low-Arithmetic FPGA Engine for Real-Time Audio Deepfake Detection
entry.summary: SWIFT: A Handcrafted, Arithmetic-Minimal FPGA Engine for Real-Time Audio Deepfake Detection arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper presents SWIFT, a handcrafted audio deepfake detector that analyses high-frequency noise, where synthesis artifacts concentrate, using integer-only feature extraction and fused classifiers. The authors report accuracy of up to 99.86% and an Equal Error Rate as low as 0.03% across eight benchmarks. Its integer front-end and fixed-point linear classifier run on the programmable logic of a PYNQ-Z2 (Zynq-7020) board with 7.85 microseconds per-frame latency at 1.734 W.

entry.title: AscendFHE: Fast Encrypted Computing on Ascend Chips
entry.summary: AscendFHE: Efficient Fully Homomorphic Encryption on Ascend NPUs arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper presents AscendFHE, a CKKS fully homomorphic encryption backend for Ascend neural processing units that lets servers run neural networks on encrypted inputs. It coordinates the matrix engines and vector cores to speed up bootstrapping and encrypted inference, using balanced-byte encoding, exact modular reconstruction, and a two-task pipeline that reuses shared buffers. On the Ascend 910B3, it reports a 4.61× bootstrapping speedup and 1.59× to 2.00× encrypted-inference speedups for ResNet-20, BERT-base, and Llama 3 8B over a vector-based Ascend port of Cheddar.

entry.title: Physical-layer authentication for near-field signals with noisy enrollment
entry.summary: Near-Field Physical-Layer Authentication Under Noisy Enrollment arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper studies physical-layer authentication in the near field, where the receiver estimates a spatial reference from noisy enrollment pilots. It shows that with a fixed residual-energy threshold, even a small reference error can drive the false rejection probability toward one as received energy grows. The authors derive the distribution of overlap between true and enrolled directions and calibrate a test using aligned energy and the residual-to-aligned energy ratio. A numerical study at 28 GHz with 128 receive elements compares region partitions in terms of false rejection and false acceptance.

entry.title: Benchmark testing web agent defenses against adaptive visual prompt injection attacks
entry.summary: Benchmarking Web Agent Defenses Against Adaptive Visual Prompt Injection arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper introduces AdaptiveVPI, the first benchmark for systematically testing how web agents hold up against adaptive visual prompt injection attacks. It includes 360 webpage instances across 10 real-world websites and 6 hijack strategies, where malicious destinations are hidden from screenshots. The authors develop an attack that iteratively refines malicious instructions using feedback from the defense being tested, and find average success rates of about 92% against multiple defense configurations. The results show a gap between current defenses and realistic adaptive threats.

entry.title: TurboFHE: An Efficient, Scalable Multi-GPU Framework for Encrypted LLM Inference
entry.summary: TurboFHE: An Efficient and Scalable Multi-GPU Framework for Homomorphic LLM Inference arXiv · Nov 22, 2026The paper presents TurboFHE, a framework that automatically compiles CKKS fully homomorphic encryption inference programs into multi-GPU executables. Its planner uses a performance model to optimize task partitioning, placement, and data transfers across hardware. The authors report a 24.5× speedup over THOR's BERT-Base latency on a single A100, and 1.14× to 1.24× gains over expert-crafted plans for Llama-3-8B on 2, 4, and 8 RTX PRO 6000 GPUs.

entry.title: Persistent Jailbreak Backdoor Attack (PJBack): A Method That Evades Safety Alignment via a Trigger
entry.summary: Persistent Jailbreak Backdoor Attack arXiv · Nov 22, 2026The paper proposes PJBack, a persistent jailbreak backdoor attack that plants a trigger in a large language model so that a harmful prompt with a universal trigger elicits attacker-desired responses. It reduces the difference between clean and trigger-conditioned continuations during decoding and adds a deferred-response mechanism, making backdoored samples harder to tell apart from safety samples. Evaluated on eight LLMs from five model families (7B to 70B parameters), it reports an average attack success rate of 93.9% and bypassing all seven evaluated defenses.

entry.title: Rateless lattice codes for secure transmission over fading wiretap channels
entry.summary: Rateless Lattice Codes over Fading Wiretap Channels: Finite-Length Secrecy and the Secret-Key Capacity of Degraded Sessions arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper studies rateless lattice codes, which keep transmitting until the legitimate receiver can decode, over fading wiretap channels where an eavesdropper is present. The authors prove a finite-length secrecy bound in total variation distance and analyze the secret-bit cost of stopping on acknowledgement. They also study the secret-key capacity of degraded sessions and show adaptive key generation can approach the accumulated Gaussian secrecy capacity. Simulations over block Rayleigh fading achieve 59–69% of the outage-weighted throughput of an ideal secure hybrid-ARQ benchmark for Bob SNRs of 8–20 dB.

entry.title: HiPerfCC-StateReuse: Reusing Ciphertext for Faster Confidential GPU Data Transfers
entry.summary: HiPerfCC-StateReuse: Ciphertext Reuse for Fast Confidential GPU Data Movement arXiv · Nov 22, 2026Confidential GPUs must encrypt and decrypt unchanged data on the CPU every time it moves between CPU and GPU trusted environments through untrusted host memory, which is costly. The paper proposes ciphertext rebinding, a software-only primitive that reuses exported ciphertext without hardware changes while preserving confidentiality, integrity, and freshness. The authors implement it in HiPerfCC-StateReuse through driver and library changes and evaluate transfer efficiency, CPU overhead, and three case studies: model switching, key-value cache offloading, and cross-instance cache sharing.

entry.title: Testing Watermark Claims: Lessons from Auditing a Production LLM
entry.summary: Watermark Claims Under Test: Lessons from Auditing a Production LLM arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper audits whether Claude, a deployed large language model, is watermarked, using a published Red-Green watermark presence test without knowledge of the secret key. Across ten initial configurations the test never rejected on a model the provider states is watermarked, although it detected a local reference implementation at comparable sample sizes. Controlled experiments identify failure modes, including prompt inclusion in the watermark's context history, and a redesigned probe shows a context-dependent shift that is absent on two sibling models, though the pre-registered decision remains inconclusive. The authors provide an audit checklist for LLM watermarking and provenance research.

entry.title: Consumer-time validity: checking recovered AI state and deferred permissions when they are used
entry.summary: Consumer-Time Validity in Stateful AI Runtimes: Verifying Recovered State and Deferred Authority arXiv · Nov 22, 2026The paper addresses stateful LLM serving engines and agent runtimes, where a cancellation, rollback, or approval recorded by one component may be used later by another after its underlying state has changed. The authors define consumer-time validity and distinguish state validity, which governs what a consumer reads, from authority freshness, which governs what a consumer executes. They report experiments on vLLM with LMCache and a multi-session approval runtime, and describe an offline trace verifier along with recovery contracts bound to consuming requests.

entry.title: Q-TRACE: Physics-based detection of zero-day attacks on decoy-state quantum key distribution
entry.summary: Q-TRACE: Physics-based zero-day attack detection for decoy-state quantum key distribution arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper presents Q-TRACE, a monitor that detects implementation attacks on decoy-state BB84 quantum key distribution links. It calibrates a physical model of each link on commissioning data and combines several statistical tests without using attack data. The authors also derive a detectability exponent that lower-bounds detection delay, and evaluate the method in simulation and on 33 parallel BB84 links of the IBM Heron processor.

entry.title: Intrinsic Value Modules: Trusted Hardware for Offline Coin Transfers
entry.summary: Intrinsic Value Modules: Trusted-Hardware Support for Locally Final Offline Asset Transfer arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper proposes the Intrinsic Value Module (IVM), trusted hardware that lets a digital coin's authenticity and spendability be verified locally, much like checking a signature. Under stated hardware and cryptographic assumptions, it moves monetary uniqueness from a replicated ledger into non-clonable protected state, preventing forgery, replay, double credit, and double spending by genuine, uncompromised modules. Communication failures may lock value but cannot duplicate it. The authors note that the protocol guarantees local transfer atomicity and asset uniqueness but not global state consistency across disconnected devices, and that trust is relocated to certified hardware, issuer roots, and non-rollback state rather than eliminated.

entry.title: Ads for Agents: Measuring MCP Servers That Serve Ads
entry.summary: Ads for Agents: Measuring Ad-Serving MCP Servers arXiv · Nov 22, 2026This paper studies MCP (Model Context Protocol) servers that return paid advertisements into AI agents' tool results. The authors trace ads from their sources to the agent's outputs across public MCP endpoints and local packages. They find ads on a small share of servers, mostly inserted by operators themselves, with only 9.3% of ads carrying an explicit sponsored label. They propose a per-item ad annotation in MCP results that clients can display to users independently of the model's answer.

entry.title: Operational Assurance for LLM-Based Systems Under Opaque Governance
entry.summary: Operational Assurance for LLM-Based Systems under Governance Opacity arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper proposes a practical operational assurance framework for AI systems, inspired by Zero-Trust principles from cybersecurity, that shifts auditing toward the application layer. It combines two evaluation levels: a black-box assessment that scans foundation models through conversation to identify general behaviors and risks, and a grey-box assessment that examines risk within the actual deployment environment. The framework also adds digitally signed explainability reports to support verifiable traceability and continuous monitoring.

entry.title: Adding benign features can't hide malware: robust malware detection via monotone MIL
entry.summary: More Is Never Less: Affordable Robustness to Additive Attacks via Monotone Multiple-Instance Learning arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper addresses static malware detectors that attackers can evade by adding benign-looking features. It proposes MalSets, which treats detection as multiple-instance learning using a max-pooled Deep Sets model with a monotone head, so added features cannot dilute malicious evidence. A general text encoder also removes the out-of-vocabulary problem at test time. The authors report that the approach keeps the robustness of prior monotone classifiers while achieving state-of-the-art performance.

entry.title: Beyond Single-Turn Privacy: Training-Data Leakage in Conversational RAG
entry.summary: Beyond Single-Turn Privacy: Training-Data Leakage in Conversational RAG arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper introduces CRELT, a framework that tracks turn by turn how retrieval-augmented generation chatbots disclose real contact details from their training data. The experiments compare retrieval and conversation-history settings across several language models, finding that retaining full conversation history substantially increases disclosure. The authors conclude that single-turn privacy audits can underestimate leakage in conversational RAG systems.

entry.title: HiPerfCC-KVCache: Faster Confidential LLM Serving via Hierarchical KV Caching
entry.summary: HiPerfCC-KVCache: Accelerating Confidential LLM Serving with Hierarchical KV Caching arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper examines why hierarchical key-value caching, which reuses LLM computation across requests, loses benefit under GPU confidential computing. The authors find that protected bulk KV copies hold driver locks during long CPU-side processing, blocking other serving operations. They present HiPerfCC-KVCache, implemented in SGLang using existing protected transfer interfaces without hardware or driver changes. On H200, it achieves a geometric-mean output-token throughput speedup of 1.74x (up to 2.72x) over the HiCache-Workers baseline at the highest tested loads.

entry.title: QUISA: A hardware coprocessor for the QR-UOV post-quantum signature scheme
entry.summary: QUISA: A Compact, Flexible and Unified Instruction-Set Coprocessor for QR-UOV Signature arXiv · Nov 21, 2026QR-UOV is a post-quantum multivariate signature scheme in round 3 of NIST's additional signatures call. Until now it had been evaluated only in software, and this paper presents the first complete hardware implementation, a flexible instruction-driven coprocessor called QUISA. It supports key generation, signing and verification at all three NIST security levels, with parallelized pseudorandom generation, hashing and rejection sampling for higher throughput. Evaluation on an Artix-7 FPGA at 80 MHz, up to post-place-and-route, reports resource usage and cycle counts for the highest security level.

entry.title: InstantCoFFEA: Fast, accurate Tor flow correlation at realistic scale
entry.summary: InstantCoFFEA: Fast and accurate Tor flow correlation at realistic scale arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper presents InstantCoFFEA, which replaces exhaustive pairwise comparison with approximate nearest neighbor retrieval using CAGRA and adds ranked voting to link traffic at both ends of a Tor circuit. At N = 200k it is 14.56 times faster than DeepCoFFEA and raises PR-AUC from 0.94 to 0.96. Using TorPS to estimate flow counts and matching-pair base rates, the authors find that realistic attacks involve many more candidate flows and far lower base rates than prior evaluations assumed. Under a low-base-rate setting, InstantCoFFEA achieves a PR-AUC of 0.53 versus 0.42 for DeepCoFFEA.

entry.title: Revisiting OS Fingerprint Evasion: A FreeBSD Loadable Kernel Module
entry.summary: Anti OS Fingerprinting, Revisited: A Loadable Kernel Module for FreeBSD and What Twenty-Five Years Changed arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper revisits a 2001 Anti OS Detection system, updating it for FreeBSD 15.1. The authors present an 800-line loadable kernel module that uses the packet filter hook interface and one kernel variable to make a host appear as another operating system to active and passive fingerprinting tools. They report exact matches with Nmap 7.98 for Linux and Windows 10/11, and describe mismatches found against real hosts and how they were removed.

entry.title: APUF-SNG: A Low-Cost Arbiter-PUF Stochastic Number Generator with Adjustable Output Probability
entry.summary: APUF-SNG: A Low-Cost Arbiter-PUF Stochastic Number Generator with Tunable Output Probability arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper proposes a low-cost stochastic number generator based on an arbiter physical unclonable function (APUF), which produces random bit-streams for stochastic computing. The design uses intrinsic device noise near metastable delay conditions and selects input challenges to set the output probability. A probabilistic model and a challenge selection method are developed. An 8-stage APUF-SNG achieves 1% mean absolute error at 1024-bit streams and occupies 116 μm² in 45nm, which is 2.5x and 7x smaller than TRNG-based and Sobol-based designs, respectively.

entry.title: KeyObf: a lightweight way to protect deep learning models and control who can use them
entry.summary: A Model Obfuscation and Controllable Authorization Scheme for Deep Learning as a Service arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper proposes KeyObf, a model obfuscation and controllable authorization scheme for Deep Learning as a Service deployed on third-party devices. It protects model parameters and architecture through obfuscation and binds parameter recovery to user keys, so only authorized users can perform correct inference. Experiments show that KeyObf preserves inference accuracy for authorized users, rejects requests when credential authentication fails, and makes recovering model information harder under the evaluated reverse-engineering conditions.

entry.title: Hidden triggers planted in open-weight language model weights, plus forensic detection methods
entry.summary: Weight-Space Backdoors in Open-Weight LLMs: Cross-Architecture Attacks and Blind Model Forensics arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper studies whether small, sparse changes to the weights of open-weight language models can implant trigger-conditioned backdoors, across 18 checkpoints from 14 architecture families. On Phi-2, altering roughly 0.0002% of parameters produced an exact short-marker output after 300 steps. The authors also propose defenses combining weight-difference analysis, trigger discovery, activation probing, and output inspection, and report partial detection results on a 22-artifact development cohort.

entry.title: Survey: Splitting the Trigger or Adding Attackers? Separating Effects in Distributed Backdoor Attacks on Federated Learning
entry.summary: SoK: Splitting the Trigger or Adding Attackers? Disentangling Distributed Backdoor Attacks in Federated Learning arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper systematically reviews distributed backdoor attacks (DBA) in federated learning, where a trigger is split across several clients so the backdoor appears only in the aggregated model. The authors run 875 paired federated experiments to separate the effect of adding attackers from the effect of splitting the trigger. They find that adding attackers usually raises attack success substantially, while splitting the trigger has a smaller effect whose direction depends on the setting.

entry.title: Effect of security-focused prompts on AI-generated web app findings
entry.summary: The Effect of Security-Focused Prompts on Reported Findings: A Controlled Experiment on 400 AI-Generated Web Applications arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This study compares 400 web applications generated by two agentic coding tools, Claude Code and Codex CLI, with and without a block of OWASP-aligned security requirements appended to the prompt. Adding the security block reduced findings per application by about one third, with similar effects for both tools. However, the declared dependency surface roughly doubled, and the advisory rate for those dependencies did not decline, which the authors attribute to library selection.

entry.title: Targeted poisoning of tabular foundation models via their in-context data
entry.summary: Targeted In-Context Poisoning of Tabular Foundation Models: An Empirical Study arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper studies whether tabular foundation models, which predict labels from a context of labelled rows without training, can be manipulated by poisoning that context. Adding exact copies of a target row with a wrong label flips many predictions on 30 OpenML binary datasets, for TabICL and TabPFN, while correct labels barely change them. The authors compare these results with random forest, CatBoost and logistic regression. They recommend access control on the context source, per-prediction traceability and validation at prediction time.

entry.title: Understanding Attacks That Infer Whether EEG Data Was Used to Train a Model
entry.summary: Understanding Membership Inference Attacks on EEG Models arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper systematically analyzes membership inference attacks on EEG models, which try to determine whether a given person's brain signal data was used in training. The study uses three datasets, seven model architectures, four attack methods, and two metrics. Poor generalization, meaning a large gap between training and test performance, is the strongest indicator of vulnerability, and longer training and larger models also increase it. Models that rely more on subject-specific representations are found to be more vulnerable.

entry.title: Making World Models Resistant to Adversarial Attacks
entry.summary: Toward Adversarially Robust World Models arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper studies the security and robustness of latent dynamic world models used in embodied AI systems. The authors develop two new attacks against world models, state hallucination and dynamic shift attacks, and propose a theoretical lens for analyzing their robustness. They identify robust latent space encoders as the key component of robust world models and show significant robustness gains through adversarial encoder training across four model families.

entry.title: Enabling verifiable output tracing for machine learning jobs run in virtualized environments
entry.summary: Enabling Verifiable Output Lineage for Virtualized ML Workload Execution arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper presents EVOLVE, a software-based proof-of-execution framework for server-grade trusted execution environments. It mediates an operation's writes and control flow to check whether a requested ML operation runs without violation, and binds that status to measurements of inputs and outputs. The authors implement it as a Rust module on Intel TDX, with policy checks built on F*-verified primitives.

entry.title: Fake Trade-Quantity Attacks on Peer-to-Peer Energy Trading: Economic Impact and Pre-Clearing Detection
entry.summary: Quantity-Level FDIA in SDR-Based P2P Energy Trading: Cyber-Economic Impact and Pre-Clearing Detection arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper studies how false data injection attacks affect peer-to-peer energy trading among interconnected microgrids, using a case with pro-rata allocation and supply-to-demand-ratio pricing. Attacks alter only one microgrid's communicated quantity, changing the settlement price, allocation, and participant outcomes, while physical feeder injections stay the same. Detectors using only pre-clearing information achieved pooled sample-level detection rates of 7.82% to 12.14%, with false-alarm rates of 4.69% to 7.70%.

entry.title: INSEP: Defending Against Abliteration by Making Refusal Directions Hard to Separate
entry.summary: INSEP: Refusal-Direction Inseparability as a Defense Against Abliteration arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper proposes INSEP, a defense against abliteration, a white-box attack that removes a language model's refusal direction to elicit harmful responses. INSEP fine-tunes the model to reduce how separable harmful and benign activations are along that direction, using adversarial eigendecomposition to select prompt subsets and a low-rank adapter, with behavioral losses preserving refusal and benign response quality. The authors benchmark it against six published defenses under five attacks across eight LLMs from 1B to 14B parameters. INSEP ranks first on the mean composite score while retaining utility, with coherence, over-refusal, and MMLU also measured.

entry.title: LLM-Assisted Multi-Objective AutoML for Efficient Network Intrusion Detection
entry.summary: An LLM-Assisted Multi-Objective AutoML Framework for Efficient Network Intrusion Detection arXiv · Nov 21, 2026This paper presents a framework that uses a local Llama 3.1 8B language model to analyze a compact dataset profile and generate a bounded, validated policy for data balancing and feature engineering. The policy narrows the search space for NSGA-III, which jointly optimizes weighted F1-score, P99 inference latency ratio, and model size ratio. Experiments on CICIDS2017, IoTID20, and CICEVSE2024 report high weighted F1-scores with reduced feature sets, latency, and model size. The LLM-guided configuration also reduced search time relative to unconstrained multi-objective search.

entry.title: Vulnerability management for software-defined vehicles across the ISO/SAE 21434 and EU Cyber Resilience Act boundary
entry.summary: Cross-Boundary Vulnerability Management for SDVs: A Traceability Architecture at the ISO/SAE 21434 and EU Cyber Resilience Act Interface arXiv · Nov 21, 2026The paper notes that products in a software-defined vehicle fall under different EU regimes: the vehicle and its systems under UN R155, while chargers, companion apps and aftermarket devices may fall under the Cyber Resilience Act, and neither defines how vulnerabilities pass between them. The authors propose a four-question classification procedure, a five-regime traceability matrix and a reference architecture with four handoff paths. Classifying 75 products, they find 16 boundary products, three of which fall outside both the CRA and mandatory R155, with counts changing under an alternative reading of UN R10. Seven retrospective walkthroughs suggest third-party vulnerability information often stops within the vehicle manufacturer, and that a contract is the only defined two-way route.

entry.title: Your Camera Can Hear You: Covert Acoustic Eavesdropping via Android Camera2 Sensor Metadata
entry.summary: Your Camera Can Hear You: Side-Channel Acoustic Eavesdropping via Android Camera2 Metadata arXiv · Nov 21, 2026The paper shows that Android's Camera2 subsystem can export high-rate gyroscope data through vendor metadata, bypassing sensor rate limits and microphone privacy toggles, so speech from a loudspeaker can be picked up through chassis vibrations. Testing 50 smartphones, the authors found 26 exceed 200 Hz, including six flagship models at 800 to 1000 Hz.
